newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Islamic Bank 1996 profits up.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Islamic Bank 1996 profits up.

text.p: Jordan Islamic Bank said on Tuesday its 1996 net profits rose 22 percent to 3.84 million dinars ($5.42 million) despite an overall slowdown in commercial banking business.
While net profits stood at 3.15 million dinars, the bank's 1996 pre-tax profits for 1996 rose to 5.6 million dinars against 3.8 million dinars in 1995, the bank's balance sheet showed.
The bank's largest shareholder is Saudi Dellah Baraka Islamic financial group, which has to keep within a 49.9 percent ceiling for foreign ownership.

The bank said it maintained healthy results despite a worse business climate in 1996 which was influenced by both political uncertainty over Middle East peace and a continued tight monetary policy to bolster the dinar.
Total investment profits, before tax deductions and allocations, rose slightly to 33.98 million dinars at end of 1996 compared to 33.40 million dinars at end of 1995, the bank said.
The bank, the country's only Islamic investment financial institution, saw a drop in its total balance sheet in 1996 to 618.65 million dinars compared with 621.9 million dinars in 1995.

Its deposits shrunk to 508.59 million dinars in 1996 against 514.9 million dinars in 1995. The bank said this was part of a general slowdown in deposit growth by the banking sector last year because of stagnant in business activity.
Shareholders rights -- capital and reserves -- rose in 1996 to 43.78 million dinars from 41.97 million dinars in 1995.
